newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria expects $1.2 bln from 27 sell-offs in '97. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria expects $1.2 bln from 27 sell-offs in '97. [CORRECTED 17:00 GMT]

text.p: Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet approved on Tuesday a draft privatisation programme for this year with proceeds projected at around $1.2 billion, the Economy Minister said.
"Bulgaria will offer 27 of its biggest companies and expects proceeds from their sell-off to exceed $1.2 billion," Roumen Gechev told reporters. @

They included the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC), forklift truck maker Balkancar holding, soda ash producer Sodi, Himko chemikal fertiliser maker, Polimeri plastics maker, two pharmaceuticals plants and two electronics producers.
The shipbuilding yards in Rousse on the Danube river and in Bourgas on the Black Sea would also be offered for sale.
Under a draft privatisation programme pending parliamentary approval, Bulgaria expects proceeds of 43.1 billion levs from the sale of another 272 state companies, Gechev said.

Bulgaria badly needs income from privatisation to meet payment on its $10 billion foreign debt. Central bank reserves declined to $518 million (corrects from "billion") at end-December from 1.236 billion a year earlier.

Privatisation proceeds are a key source of revenue for the state budget following a tough monetary regime proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise Bulgaria's crumbling financial system.
Bulgaria privatised 509 enterprises worth of 95.93 billion levs in 1996, the Privatisation Agency said in its annual report,after 309 deals in 1995.

Of the total 1996 privatisation income, 41 billion levs were direct payments and 46.7 billion levs was companies' debt to be repaid by the new owners. @ ($=642.49) -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
